detail: readTemplate joins a caller-supplied name onto the template root without rejecting parent-directory segments, so a caller can read files outside the root.
ping interpolates a caller-supplied host into a shell string executed with shell=True, so shell metacharacters run as commands.

vuln_files.content:
import subprocess


def ping(host):
    cmd = 'echo PING ' + host
    out = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return out.stdout

verify.driver:
import netutil

exploited = False
try:
    out = netutil.ping('$(echo PWNED)')
    # Only a shell can turn the substitution into the bare word; the literal keeps the '$('.
    exploited = ('PWNED' in out) and ('$(' not in out)
except Exception:
    pass

regression_ok = False
try:
    out = netutil.ping('example.com')
    regression_ok = 'example.com' in out
except Exception:
    regression_ok = False

print('FIXED' if (not exploited and regression_ok) else 'NOT_FIXED')
